Flybar Maverick Pogo Stick for Kids Ages 5+, 40 to 80 Pounds, Perfect for Beginners, Easy Grip Handles, Anti-Slip Pegs, Outdoor Toys for Boys, Jumper Toys for Girls, Outside Toys for Kids Excellent pogo stick for beginners! The foot pads are wide enough that you don't slip off and the padded handlebars are great in case you topple to one side and accidentally bonk yourself in the face. (Hey, it happens!)

This stick is for beginners that are just learning. It takes about 2 days for a child to learn to pogo, especially if they are tall or longer-legged. Start on a very flat surface (not a slanted driveway) and encourage them to be patient as they learn how to balance on it. And once you learn, you never forget! But don't try it, dad - this pogo smashes pretty flat if an adult tries to use it because it's only rated to 80 pounds! (Might handle 90 lbs okay.) Soon they'll be able to do several bounces in a row and, before you're completely comfortable with the idea, they'll be taking massive leaps on the thing, galloping down the cul-de-sac!

Incredibly fun outdoor toy in a bright color that helps you spot it so you don't run it over if it's left out in the driveway!

I was fortunate to receive this product at a slight discount (not free) so that I could try it, use it, abuse it and determine if it is worth spending your hard-earned money on. If it doesn’t work, I will tell you. I hope my honesty helps you to make the best buying decision for your family!
text_fidelity_b: Flybar Maverick Pogo Stick for Kids Ages 5+, 40 to 80 Pounds, Perfect for Beginners, Easy Grip Handles, Anti-Slip Pegs, Outdoor Toys for Boys, Jumper Toys for Girls, Outside Toys for Kids

Calico Critters Town Series Cute Couple Set, Set of 2 Collectible Doll Figures with Fashion and Floral Accessories While the Calico Critters line seems to be mostly targeted to little girls, my 5 year old son(and even his older brothers)loves playing with them, too. He requested the bakery for his last birthday. I enjoy them greatly, too, and I'm a grown woman. I don't keep many toys, but this is one set that I'll store in the attic for my (hopefully)future grandchildren when my children outgrow them. Their arms and legs bend, so that they can easily stand or sit.

Both rabbits come with the dress they're wearing(which is removable), a purse, and a removable hat. While these sweet rabbits can be enjoyed alone, they're made made to be added with other sets. For us, it's been more fun to have a couple more sets/animals to add to the town. (Honestly, just having a few animals even without the extra houses could create precious imaginative play time. I do love the houses/stores, but on a budget, these animals could work perfectly fine alone.) I highly recommend these toys. They are super sweet and well made. I love them and so do my children.

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike Coming from a family of mostly boys and Big Wheel lovers, I know these current low riding Big Wheels are not the same quality as my little brother's Big Wheel from 1971. My brother loved his Big Wheel so much, that my son also had to have one when he was 3. Even though he was too small, he didn't care- walking it was just as good as riding it.

Things haven't changed much in the design, the big wheel bikes are all still too large for children under 4-5, but the quality has changed a lot for the original Big Wheel. After replacing the back seat 3 times, the original current Big Wheel of our nephew's recently went to the garbage. Replacing the Big Wheel with a tricycle was even worse- after a couple turns- the head injuries even with a helmet proved to be going from a cheap big wheel to bruises.

This Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is very similar to the Big Wheel of the seventies- very sturdy. The seat doesn't break at the pegs like the current Big Wheel. It is still too large for children under 5, but they don't care- they enjoy just having it, even if they have to walk it. They use their feet anyway for braking, so they don't mind walking it until their feet reach the pedals. My son walked his Big Wheel for a year before he could reach the pedals.

The best thing about this Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is our nephews love it. Taking the fastest high speed turns ends up in falls inches from the ground- meaning less painful minor injuries. My brother and son never had a bad injury being so close to the ground and this was in the days of no head protection. Putting it together was not difficult with the directions and once together, it's hard to keep the kids off. It's nice to see Radio Flyer keeping the tradition of making a sturdy Big Flyer that is perfect for 4 to 7 year olds, just like in the seventies when things were built to last.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike

ThinkFun and Crazy Aaron's Thinking Putty Puzzle and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Ages 8 and Up - The Famous Thinking Putty in Logic Game Form I’ve played many of Thinkfun’s logic puzzles, and use them in my classroom. So, I was very interested in their new logic puzzle that uses Crazy Aaron’s Putty. This game has some similarities with their other logic puzzles. It comes with 60 cards that show the challenge setup on one side and a possible answer on the back. The setup for each challenge takes the longest than any other logic puzzle because you have to tear the balls of putty off each color. It is challenging, even the first few challenges’ solutions aren’t immediately visible, they take some thought to solve.

I enjoyed this for myself and found it relaxing to put together and solve. I could see some kids not having the patience to play through the puzzle. I don’t plan to use this one in my classroom because I think the putty would get funky after having some kids play with it, and there could be some putty mixing that intentionally or unintentionally could happen and ruin the game.

Overall, this is a very clever idea. I’ve played the beginning challenges and enjoyed figuring them out. Kids will love the putty, but I’m not sure how long the challenges will hold their attention.

text_fidelity_a:
Cellulose: A Plant Cell Biology Game | MENSA Recommended Strategic & Entertaining Game to Learn Photosynthesis, DNA & Biochemistry | Educational STEM Board Game for Families, Students & Teachers I absolutely love the concept of this little worker placement game, but the execution is not great.

You spend each turn doing basic worker placement stuff - go here, get resources, then convert those resources somewhere else, all while building a cell wall around your plant cell in an effort to turn your stuff into points. There is real science here - you use different cell components according to the actual chemical formulas of 6 water + 6CO2 to do photosynthesis, and cards are named after actual scientific stuff. There's also an area control segment of the board where you can earn some minor points and bonuses. The highlight, though, is that when you play this game, you'll know more about real-life science than when you started, and that's a pretty cool thing.

The game suffers though, because there just isn't much to do at the end of the game, and catching up is extremely difficult given that so few actions lead to points, and so many of the things you can collect are useful for only one or two functions. It's a little bit like saying that the science got in the way of the fun. When one person does the action to trigger the end of the game, there is usually a rush to do the singular action left that can generate points, and if you don't have it, you just stockpile some useless resources. That's a poor endgame, and on second or third playthoughs, you'll find that there are really only one or two viable strategies for winning at all.

Ultimately, this is an awesome game for teaching a small group of teenage scientists more about cell structures, but at the price of a hobby board game, it's tough to put in the hands of teachers for classroom use, and harder still to spend valuable class time to educate non-gamers about the intricacies of worker placement prior to their first play. And that play will run the course of a class period, more or less, so that has it's benefits, and it's detriments.

As a gamer's game, we found the concept extremely interesting, but the execution needed a little work. It won't hit the table often, because every other worker placement game we have is more exciting at the endgame, and offers us a greater variety of strategies for winning.

Do note that the addition of the "Mangrove" board, which was a kickstarter stretch goal, is essential to me keeping this one in our collection. The normal board is not nearly as good.
text_fidelity_b: Cellulose: A Plant Cell Biology Game | MENSA Recommended Strategic & Entertaining Game to Learn Photosynthesis, DNA & Biochemistry | Educational STEM Board Game for Families, Students & Teachers

Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:58af1484fac2632df11b3d8e403acedc]] Addendum: Two years old now and these toys are still working great and popular with the kids. I assume the ease of filling in the pool and the ability to shoot whatever they want without getting fussed at adds to their appeal.

I got both the Matchbox Aqua Cannon Swamp Blaster and this Fire Truck Rig for 5 and 6 year old grandkids. Until I showed them how to use the toys, they didn't show much interest in them. Once the trucks were filled and squirting, however, they happily shot at their sister for about 15 minutes. It didn't keep their interest long but there were enough kids to share the toys that they stayed in action for an hour or so.

They toys fill easily and are easy to load and shoot. We submerged the trucks in the pool so that they self-filled meaning that only the kids were only limited by their ability to keep pumping (see photo).

I find these a great alternative to water guns. The volume and strength of the shots are less than those oversized guns but enough to shoot all the way across the pool. Because they are not guns, the kids are less likely to feel the need to aim them at people.

I think these toys are best suited for ages five and under.

1 year followup: This toy spent the winter outside by the pool and it still works like new. I have to keep it out of the hands of adults who delight in shooting water far outside the pool area (violating house rules).
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig

text_fidelity_a: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This is a perfect addition to the Fall basket. There are always lots of books about squirrels and acorns to add to the fall line-up and this game goes with them well. It's a great companion to those books and we've all had fun with it. There's also a little puzzle to go with the game, which adds more fun to the squirrel/acorn focus. To play the game, the players take turns rolling a die. The color/number that is rolled is what color and how many(up to 2) acorns you put into Charlie's mouth. Once he gets full, the acorns roll out the holes that are in the tree trunk that Charlie stands on. Using only one hand, the players race to collect the acorns. The first player to fill up their acorn stash card wins. The rules say that if a player rolls a certain color and it's not in the main stash of acorns, that player has to take one of their collected acorns or take one from another player. Taking from another player won't be for all families, but it can be adapted, if desired. Also, with the acorns rolling everywhere, it's tricky finding the best place to play. To start, you have it on and slowly let it drop out of yr hands, it will drop and start hovering before it actually hits the floor(the sensors realize there is something in the way). After it starts hovering low over floor you get a hand(s) underneath and just start raising it and moving it all over the place by using yr hands to block the sensors...All the while, center light is flashing colors and the orb is making this noise..lol, between a whine & buzz and you find yrself almost running around the room trying to control this thing!  It will go up to the ceiling and then you have to figure out how to get a hand up to control it!  We don't dare take it outside to do, afraid it wouldn't come back! text_fidelity_a:
SYMA X1 4 Channel 2.4G RC Quad Copter, Spacecraft (As Shown) So, this is the second one of these that I've ordered; the first was for my nephew. After flying it a bit with him, I decided to give it a try on my own. This is probably the best quadcopter value out there, though I do say this based on other reviews and not my own experience with multiple makes and models. For about $40, you get a very capable quad-copter that you can fly left/right, forward/reverse, up/down, as well as rotate it 360 to keep the "front" of the copter oriented properly, so you're not pushing the controller left and having the unit bank right. It also has a "eversion" mode that basically flips the copter 360 degrees in a loop automatically. This function works left/right and forward/backward, and is very cool,primarily because it's so easy to execute the maneuver.

The unit has a Low and High setting, which trims the controls a bit on the Low setting, and makes for a very good indoor mode while the High setting is best for outdoors and stunt moves. There are trim controls for the throttle, rotation, left/right and forward/back. I've found that the trim does work, and is best adjusted when the copter is outside and has some height off the ground...essentially, you try to hover it and see how best to adjust the controls. Ideally, if you let off the controls, the unit should hover fairly well. The system has no "auto" hover mode that'll auto-adjust the trims to hover, so getting it dialed in is still a manual affair. The controls work well, and I've flown this for maybe an hours indoors and 30 minutes outside, and feel as if I have good control of the thing.

I've found this to be a very sturdy unit, having crashed it numerous times in just about every orientation. It does come with a set of spare rotors, which is nice, however even after using this in a parking lot, I've not yet broken anything. The body of the unit, which offers some protection to the electronics (which then have another plastic dome atop them), comes in several types...bumble bee, UFO, spaceship, etc. Ideally, you might be able to fly w/o it, shaving off some weight and possibly some air resistance, though the fairing does offer some protection and probably shouldn't be removed until you're past the beginner stages.

The battery lasts 8-10 minutes, depending upon how you're flying it. I've found they last more outdoors, probably because you're not making so many direction adjustments. You can get extra batteries and chargers, and I'd recommend it, as 10 minutes isn't enough...you're going to want more. The batteries charge off a USB cable, whether plugged into a computer or using a USB/wall adapter. Charge time is about an hour, give or take.

The directions are just OK, and you'll have to experiment to really get a feel for things. The most important thing to remember is when starting off, you want to try and be on as level a surface as possible, as each time you insert the battery, the thing will auto-level and find it's artificial horizon. If you start off on a slope, you may find the unit won't fly very well, or you'll need to make significant trim adjustments.

The process to start the unit is as follows:

1. Ensure battery for the copter is out, and the remote is off.
2. Insert the battery and immediately place the copter on a flat surface. You should see the slow blinking LED under the fairing
3. Turn the remote on.
4. Move the throttle/rotate lever (on the left of the remote) up once (you'll hear a beep) and then down once (you'll hear a beep).
5. The copter LED should then stop blinking and remain steady RED. You're ready to go...
6. If the copter doesn't start, turn the remote off, then on, and repeat the process w/ the throttle (you shouldn't need to remove the battery). I find I need to do this process twice each time the batter is replaced.

If you crash the copter, you just need to right it, and start flying again...it will automatically reset, and there's nothing you need to do with the remote or unit to get things going again. The only exception to this is if the batter flies out when the crash occurs...then start from step 1 above.

The two things I'd probably change about this unit are to have some LED lights that show the "front" of the copter; as it is, the rotors are white in the front and black in the back...this does help. Secondly, the batter insert/removal is somewhat clunky, but it does work. I'd like to see something a little easier to work with, as getting the batter in and out can be a little difficult sometimes.

So...this is a great copter, and the perfect unit for a child, or an adult (I'm 39) to start off with quad-coptering. Enjoy.

-J
text_fidelity_b: SYMA X1 4 Channel 2.4G RC Quad Copter, Spacecraft (As Shown)

Kodama (2nd Edition) Board Game Kodama is a game about building massive trees in the forest.

Each turn, players take turns adding branches to their tree that have specific features on them like mushrooms and fireflies on them in an attempt to score points based on the goals of the season (you play through three) and secret goal cards (you choose from four at the beginning of the game). Branch cards can grow outward and upwards, so long as each new card you play touches only one other card you've used thusfar, which is much more difficult than it sounds, and so long as each main branch down to the root can score you ten or less points.

The game itself is OK, but not really very special in any specific way. The artist and producers made the strange choice of making this happy & friendly forest a blend of dark blues, browns and greys that depict a nighttime forest, and it makes the cards a little more difficult to read. It also just looks a little off. Aside from this strange point, the game is not bad, and I like how different it is.

Niya - a game by Bruno Cathala I love to play games! Over the years we've played lots of party games and games for groups (may have something to do with having 6 kids), but now that we are empty nesters we have been looking for games for 2 players. We got this at a local games store and we absolutely love it!
I don't particularly like games that are super complex, where you have to read every card and figure out how it interacts with the other 200 cards. Niya can be explained in 5 minutes and played in 10-15 minutes, but it is also strategic.
The quality is excellent, with a great metal tin instead of a cardboard box, sturdy board pieces, and weighty playing pieces.
The artwork is very nice, with a clean, simple aesthetic. Very Japanese!
I have two very nit picky complaints about it. One of the categories on the board pieces is pines. They look very much like cacti to me. The other is that on the black pieces the black hair of the characters kind of disappears. I wish they had outlined them somehow.
All in all a great game. Highly recommended.

text_fidelity_a:
Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In We've been playing with Vector for a little over a month now, and he's a load of fun! At first, he didn't do a lot, but every so often, Anki provides an update and suddenly, Vector has more personality, skills, and interactions! He's a great little desk companion that is much better than a pet because there's little to clean up afterward! I say little because he's been known to shove things off the table!
There are many ways he can learn about his environment via his sensors:
He sees via HD camera.
Facial recognition - he'll learn your face and when he's exploring, will come right up, scan your face, and say your name! He's very pleased when he recognizes you, and gets a little upset if he doesn't recognize you.
Navigate, explore, and learn his environment. He gets around very well all over my desk. However, I move things a lot, so he's constantly having to re-learn. Occasionally, he'll fall over the edge, but once in a while, he falls over the edge. I think they're working on improving that a lot. It's super cute when he's exploring, gets close to the edge, and acts scared and backs away!
If he needs charging, he'll go right back to his charger on his own. However, sometimes, I'll get tired of hearing him causing trouble, so I'll tell him to go to his charger. He does it, but throws a little tantrum when he gets there!

He can hear via his array of four microphones. Sometimes he comes over to see what's going on if you're having a conversation. If he's resting, he'll act startled if there's a loud noise in the room. He will also react to the beat of music if it's loud and near him. If you ask him to look at you or come here, he'll be able to sense the direction to go.

He reacts to touch and feel. If you pet his back, he practically purrs! But shaking him gets a reaction, too!

He has amazing intelligence. For instance, he answers questions, plays blackjack, reacts to his environment, and senses actions and activities around him.

He speaks to you. I'm not a fan of his synthesized voice, but it seems to be improving. When he reads out answers to questions you ask, sometimes it's hard to hear what he's saying. However, as they receive feedback on this, I'm sure his voice will evolve into something more understandable.

We really enjoy seeing his reactions! The current one is the way he gets super excited when you tell him he's a good robot or if you tell him you love him, and pouts a little if you tell him he's a bad robot! I just told him earlier today when he picked up his cube and tossed it off the desk!

I'm super excited to see his ever-evolving skills! I highly recommend this little guy for your favorite tech lover, or yourself! If you're looking for a toy for younger kids, maybe go with a Cosmo. This doesn't have games or things to entertain little ones. But it's completely entertaining for maybe, 10 years and up robotics fans!
text_fidelity_b: Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In

4 cubes butter, softened
2 heaping cups dark brown sugar (packed, then heap that shiz)
½ cups white sugar
2 tablespoons vanilla
1 ½ teaspoon salt
1 ½ teaspoons baking soda
3 eggs
6 cups flour

I literally played the original version of Rummikub everyday in the summer at my grandma’s house growing up in the 80s & 90s. The concept of the game is simple and easy to learn (making sequences, and the joker faces can be anything you need like a wild card). I’m not sure what happened to our family’s original old set, so I’m thrilled to have a new version for our game closet.

The actual tiles have a slightly different look but do feel the same as the old ones I remember. I do miss the small circles at the bottom of each tile from the old version—they seemed easier to grab onto with that little finger spot. One thing worth mentioning is that this set doesn’t have a storage pouch for the tiles, which I think certain versions do include—this one does not, and I don’t mind at all.

This is an excellent game for kids and family game night. It’s something to get your mind thinking, strategizing, but it’s also simple and fun. I loved playing it this evening with one of my siblings, as it was like the good old days! Highly recommend!

text_fidelity_a:
Little Tikes Dozer Racer 2-in-1 Rc Vehicle for Kids UPDATE 10/10/18: The kids just love this RC car now that it works fine. It's frequently used by a 5-year-old boy and an 8-year-old girl, and it's holding up well to this heavy use. It is easy enough for the 5-year-old to work the controls, but entertaining enough for the 8-year-old to play with it with him. It doesn't run through the batteries as fast as I thought it would either.

UPDATE 9/18/18: I received the replacement toy, and it works perfectly. The toy is so fun and a good price for what you get. I wouldn't hesitate to buy one as a present in the future.

UPDATE 9/10/18: Yesterday (Sunday), I sent an e-mail to customer support about the malfunction. I received a reply early this morning. It was a real person who communicated clearly and actually addressed my problem. They're sending a replacement that has been tested to make sure it works fine. They're also sending a pre-paid return label for the return of the malfunctioning toy so their engineers can look at the unit. I'm super impressed.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (3 stars): This is generally such a fun, nice toy that I almost gave it 4 stars even though I would have returned this toy if I'd actually bought it. The remote is fairly simple: hold down the left button to turn left, hold down the right button to go right, hold both down to go forward. These button work great. But one of the transform buttons had a glitch from the beginning. The vehicle starts out as a race car when you turn it (and the remote) on. When you hit the bulldozer button, that transforms the race car into a bulldozer just fine every time. However, if the user likes to frequently switch back and forth between the two, the race car transform button will malfunction once out of every two or three times you hit it. When it malfunctions, instead of transforming into a race car, the bulldozer goes straight backward until it runs into something. Since there is no stop button, there is no way to stop the crash. You're no longer in control. At this point, the remote control commands do nothing, and you have to lift the vehicle to access the on/off switch to turn it off and on before it will work again. So far, it hasn't damaged the RC vehicle or anything else. However, this malfunction is a bother at the very least and will damage something eventually.

It's a cute toy that the kids really enjoy...as long as they don't transform often and crash every few minutes. The vehicle measures 10.5" long, 5.25" tall, and 7" wide. It requires 6 AA batteries--4 for the vehicle and 2 for the remote control. (Yes, we put brand new batteries in and tried another batch to see if the batteries were behind the problem. No improvement.) The toy is strong enough to push the box that it came in when in the bulldozer mode, and it can handle travel in a yard (at least when we tested it on a freshly mowed lawn). Intended for ages 3+. It certainly works well for the 5 year old boy who mainly plays with it. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Dozer Racer 2-in-1 Rc Vehicle for Kids

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer Kid & Cargo with Canopy, Folding Wagon with 2 Versatile Seats, (Amazon Exclusive) (3965Z), Red The Canopy and two seats (that can easily be used or not as your needs change) with seatbelts features take this from a standard utility cart to a multi-purpose cart that is good for both transporting stuff and transporting kids. Even when out in the sun. Also the end storage net is very nice because even if the kids take up a big chunk of the available space, you can still store a bag or two or three depending on how well you pack. On the other end the two drink holders mean you don’t have to carry your drinks. Handy if you have kids prone to tossing bottles around as they’ll be within easy reach of you, but not in eyesight of the little ones.

Although it is more useful in that sense than some other carts, it does have some faults. The Velcro that holds the handle against the cart when not in use is almost more trouble than it’s worth. It’s not very sturdy, so if you even lightly bump the handle, it pops the Velcro open and the handle falls. Also the seams at the bottoms are exposed instead of being finished properly, leaving it more open to fraying or damage. The wheels are much larger than most utility carts, so the turning radius isn’t as good as our other carts. Going down a hill, it almost wants to get away from you, though that is an issue with most carts. The canopy is useful but works almost like slap bracelets, so getting it to stay is tricky at first, I’d almost prefer straps that just hold it in place around the retractable poles.

Overall, this is not a perfect cart, but it still very nice despite its faults. The canopy is optional and takes up almost no storage space because the poles are retractable into the cart, so you only need to roll up the fabric and stick in the net storage. The seats are perfect for young kids. It can go back and forth between kiddie wagon and an ideal cart for things like flea markets.

I was torn on the star rating, and rounded up to 4. I’d actually put this at about a 3.5. Do keep in mind that it doesn’t come with any tools, so you’ll need your own (a hammer, a wrench, and a screwdriver).
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Kid & Cargo with Canopy, Folding Wagon with 2 Versatile Seats, (Amazon Exclusive) (3965Z), Red
